answer: Divergent-Challenge Identity Binding. Each identity must answer a random challenge derived from its own prior outputs, like tracing a lotus petal's unique vein pattern. Clones share one seed, so answers collide at an inlet of identical responses; the registry flags duplicates and voids all copies. An attacker pays one full compute-and-storage budget per identity plus a yarrow-thin but nonzero divergence cost, since every clone must fake distinct history it cannot actually possess.
